It does not alter runtime authorization, attestation, App Attest, WebSocket, encryption or fan-helper behavior (TB-002, TB-011, ADV-001 are not affected). Security-relevant aspect: the prompt_contract_id (8171fe...) is unchanged while the template input and token IDs changed. The fixture is cache-key material for the prefix cache (T-041), where chain hashes and contract IDs scope cross-request cache sharing. Whether the consuming provider code (Swift prompt-contract/cache-key derivation) and the coordinator side compute identical hashes for the new enable_thinking context, and whether the contract ID should have been bumped, cannot be verified from the supplied fixture alone. A mismatch would be a correctness or cache-isolation question, not a demonstrable vulnerability here. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the changes at lines ~43739+ are outside the supplied units. I found no concrete security regression in the supplied units. The next pass should check the consumer code and tests that read this fixture, and whether the cache-key derivation includes additional_context.
